name: Dag Nasty
label: Dischord
lede: Four singers, one guitarist who never left, and a 1986 record that taught hardcore how to carry a tune without losing its nerve.

eras.title: Minor Threat's guitarist wants a melody
eras.text: Minor Threat was done and Brian Baker had songs that were faster than pop and catchier than anything hardcore was allowing itself. He pulled a rhythm section out of Bloody Mannequin Orchestra and a singer out of the DC scene, and by Halloween they had a whole album on tape.

years.h: Brian Baker builds Dag Nasty out of Bloody Mannequin Orchestra
years.p: Drummer [[Colin Sears|c9bbc03c-06bf-4c37-9f54-e95b51aede4c]] and bassist [[Roger Marbury|c24bb563-e743-4478-9380-fe877ca4031f]] come over from Bloody Mannequin Orchestra, and [[Shawn Brown|e39556a4-0d8f-4138-bc18-a54d3a66eefe]] sings. Brian Baker, ex-[[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], is the one with the plan.

eras.title: Three singers in one year
eras.text: Can I Say, the record that made Dag Nasty's name, happened in a hurry, with Boston singer Dave Smalley, who wasn't going to stay. By the end of 1986 the band had lost him, toured half the country with Peter Cortner, found through a classified ad, and quit.

years.h: Boston's Dave Smalley replaces Shawn Brown
years.p: [[Dave Smalley|c637a12d-5f55-4b83-bef0-a56b3c1e326c]] of Boston straight-edge band [[DYS|f012c04d-96ca-47dd-9359-3bb11fed88b5]] takes the mic from Shawn Brown, and a hardcore shouter is now fronting the most tuneful band in D.C.

years.h: Dag Nasty live at the Electric Banana, Pittsburgh
years.p: Dag Nasty's show at the Pittsburgh club is taped. Four live tracks from that night later ride along as bonus cuts on the Can I Say CD.

years.h: Can I Say · Dischord No. 19
years.p: Dag Nasty's debut, recut at Inner Ear with Ian MacKaye producing and Dave Smalley singing. Brian Baker's MXR chorus pedal, found lying around the studio, ends up all over the record.
years.xp:
Brian Baker played a '70s Les Paul goldtop through a Marshall. Eight of the songs had been around since the Shawn Brown session and were, in Baker's words to Guitar World, slightly tarted up for the new take. The borrowed chorus pedal is the secret ingredient: it gives the guitars that wide, ringing sheen that set the record apart from the DC hardcore around it.

The album's reach runs long. Its songs are cited in histories of emo, Circles turned up on a Tony Hawk game soundtrack, and Blink-182's Travis Barker has the title tattooed on his chest.

q: Our singer decides he's going to go do graduate school.
years.h: Dave Smalley quits for NYU before the Descendents tour
years.p: Dag Nasty land the opening slot on a big summer run with the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]]. Before it starts, Dave Smalley leaves to attend grad school at New York University.
years.xp:
It was the break a young band waits for, and it came apart on the calendar. Dave Smalley chose school, and Brian Baker was left with dates on the books and nobody to sing them.

The fix was Peter Cortner, found through a classified ad, and his voice changed Dag Nasty's direction for the next two years.

years.h: Dag Nasty find Peter Cortner through a want ad
years.p: Dag Nasty places an ad in a local paper and finds [[Peter Cortner|66e99d7d-3c1e-429b-a95c-5591f9278616]]. He learns the set and tours with the Descendents across half the United States.

years.h: Dag Nasty fold after the Descendents tour
years.p: Home from the Descendents tour and a few local shows, Dag Nasty calls it. Brian Baker heads to Los Angeles and starts Doggy Style with Descendents bassist [[Doug Carrion|bdc25394-8356-4bcd-9118-520f17af9333]].

years.h: Live at Chevy Chase Community Center, March 21, 1986
yt: Live at Chevy Chase Community Center, March 21, 1986

eras.title: Wig out, then Field Day
eras.text: Brian Baker and Doug Carrion came back east and rebuilt Dag Nasty around Peter Cortner's voice, which pushed the band further toward pop. Two albums, Wig Out at Denko's and Field Day, a move off Dischord to Giant Records, and then the original run was over.

years.h: Dag Nasty re-forms with Doug Carrion on bass
years.p: Brian Baker, Peter Cortner, Colin Sears and Doug Carrion restart Dag Nasty. Bassist Roger Marbury declines to rejoin.

years.h: Wig Out at Denko's · Dischord No. 26
years.p: Dag Nasty's second album and Peter Cortner's first, recorded at Inner Ear in March with Ian MacKaye and Don Zientara: brighter, poppier, still fast. Alternative Press later put it in the emo canon.
years.xp: The title is a D.C. in-joke: the band's own site says Denko was a guy from Washington who threw house parties.

years.h: Dag Nasty's All Ages Show 7" on Giant
years.p: A single for Giant Records, the label that would release Dag Nasty's next album, Field Day.

years.h: Colin Sears out, Scott Garrett in for Field Day
years.p: Founding drummer Colin Sears is gone by the time Dag Nasty cuts its third album, Field Day, for Giant. Scott Garrett plays on it.

years.h: Live at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach CA, March 27, 1987
yt: Live at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach CA, March 27, 1987

years.h: Field Day · Giant Records
years.p: Dag Nasty's third and most ambitious album: pop hooks, hardcore speed, a cover of [[The Ruts|a2f938aa-1aa3-474b-a070-762067274eab]] and a remake of Under Your Influence from Can I Say.
years.xp: Robert Christgau gave it an A minus. According to Wikipedia, it sold more than 30,000 copies in its first year.

years.h: Dag Nasty's first run ends
years.p: Dag Nasty splits shortly after the Field Day tour: three singers, two bass players and three drummers in four years, by the band's own count.
years.xp: In 2009 Brian Baker was still calling Peter Cortner a really good lyricist and talking about another record with him.

eras.title: Dale Nixon plays guitar
eras.text: Brian Baker went off to play hard rock in Junkyard and signed a contract that followed him back to punk. The Can I Say line-up made one more album anyway, Four on the Floor, with Baker credited as Dale Nixon, and then he joined Bad Religion, the job that defined the rest of his career.

years.h: Baker goes hard rock with [[Junkyard|0388b116-a688-4122-bfb7-ca9a1f4aef1a]]
years.p: Brian Baker and Chris Gates, formerly of Austin's Big Boys, start the Los Angeles hard rock band Junkyard. A long way from Inner Ear.

years.h: 85-86 collects early Dag Nasty
years.p: Selfless Records puts out a set of Dag Nasty's pre-Can I Say recordings.

years.h: Four on the Floor · Epitaph
years.p: Dave Smalley, Roger Marbury and Colin Sears back with Brian Baker, cut in Los Angeles in summer 1991 with [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]] producing. Baker is credited as Dale Nixon because he was under contract to Junkyard.
years.xp:
Dale Nixon is a punk in-joke with a history: it's the alias Greg Ginn used for his bass parts on [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]'s My War. Baker borrowing it for a contractual workaround is about as DC-to-LA as a credit line gets.

The Washington Post called the album first-rate. It was the Can I Say band, minus Baker's name on the sleeve.

years.h: Brian Baker picks [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]] over R.E.M.
years.p: Brian Baker turns down a touring spot with R.E.M. and takes Brett Gurewitz's place in Bad Religion. He's still there three decades on.

eras.title: Back to the basement
eras.text: Dag Nasty came home to Inner Ear for a full-length that sounded like hardcore again, then Dischord opened the vault on the session that started everything.

years.h: Minority of One · Revelation Records
years.p: Dag Nasty, with Dave Smalley singing again, records at Inner Ear with Don Zientara and former Minor Threat bassist [[Steve Hansgen|cd469927-13a8-4d0b-8898-01c6856f5878]] producing, and the tempos go back up. Reviews were split: Drowned in Sound liked it, Pitchfork didn't.

years.h: Dag With Shawn: the shelved 1985 session, out at last
years.p: Dag Nasty cut nine songs with Shawn Brown at Inner Ear on Halloween 1985, then shelved them when Brown left. Dischord restored the master tapes and released them as No. 168 in 2010.
years.xp:
[[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produced the session in Don Zientara's Arlington basement. Dischord's notes say the album was shelved after Brown departed, and in early 1986 the band recut it with Dave Smalley as Can I Say.

Brown went on to front [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], one of the harder-edged D.C. bands of the next few years, and came back to Dag Nasty on his own terms in 2012.

eras.title: The first singer gets his turn
eras.text: Dag Nasty's original line-up with Shawn Brown, once a footnote, became the working band. The D.C. punk documentary Salad Days brought them to the stage, and a new session at Inner Ear gave Shawn Brown his first Dag Nasty release that didn't come out of the archive.

years.h: Dag Nasty's original four reunite at the Black Cat
years.p: Shawn Brown, Brian Baker, Roger Marbury and Colin Sears, announced in October as their first show together since 1985, play D.C.'s Black Cat for Salad Days: The DC Punk Revolution. [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]] are on the bill too.

years.h: Cold Heart: Shawn Brown's first new Dag Nasty songs
years.p: Dag Nasty's original four recorded Cold Heart and Wanting Nothing at Inner Ear in December 2015 with Ian MacKaye and Don Zientara. Dischord released them as No. 184, three decades after Dave Smalley replaced Brown.

years.h: Dag Nasty tours Europe, Las Vegas and Asbury Park
years.p: Dag Nasty plays a European run, Punk Rock Bowling in Las Vegas, and a June 11 date in Asbury Park, New Jersey.
